assessments.task_description:
There will be 3 in-class reflexive statements throughout the semester.

The short reflexive statements (max 200 words) are a response to one of the two questions given in the lecture during the assessment time. The questions relate to the course content, and answers should draw on lecture materials, readings, and/or tutorial discussions. These are in-class pen and paper assessments, undertaken during scheduled lecture times.

Marks from all reflexive statements will be aggregated to comprise 35%.

assessments.task_description:
In groups of 2-3 you will research, prepare and present a 10-minute presentation, and a 2-minute Q&A. This presentation is an exercise to decipher the cultural significance of your chosen statue, museum, mural, film or Wikipedia page and to critically evaluate how and why it tells stories about the past in the way that it does.  

Use of generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) or Machine Translation (MT) 

Use of generative AI and MT is restricted to: 

-       Brainstorming

-       Searching for relevant literature

-       Improving grammar/spelling

You are not to use generative AI or MT tools for any other purpose except the above tasks. Refer to instructions included on Blackboard about using AI tools with integrity.

All essays must include the AI Acknowledgment Coversheet Template to declare if and how AI or MT has been used. 

A failure to declare the use of generative AI or MT may constitute student misconduct under the Student Code of Conduct. 

To pass this assessment, students will be required to demonstrate detailed comprehension of their written submission independent of AI and MT tools.

assessments.task_description:
You are to research and write an essay on a critical issue in Australian sport history. This essay is an exercise in taking the historical understanding you have gained about a variety of Australian Sport History issues and applying it to a specific case, event, or person. This essay is about you choosing a topic and exploring it historically.

The essay tests your ability to analyse and communicate about historical issues using primary and secondary sources by asking you to

  • Explain the issue, situating the primary sources in their historical context.
  • Explain and apply concepts – combining knowledge gained from the course and your own original research – to analyse the chosen case study with secondary sources.


Use of generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) or Machine Translation (MT) 

Use of generative AI or MT is restricted to 

-       Brainstorming

-       Searching for relevant literature

-       Improving grammar/spelling

You are not to use generative AI or MT tools for any other purpose except the above tasks. Refer to instructions included on Blackboard about using AI tools with integrity.

All essays must include the AI Acknowledgment Coversheet Template to declare if and how AI or MT has been used. 

A failure to declare the use of generative AI or MT may constitute student misconduct under the Student Code of Conduct. 

To pass this assessment, students will be required to demonstrate detailed comprehension of their written submission independent of AI and MT tools.
